MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  APRIL 25, 2017

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order at 7:04 p.m. in the City Council Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by
MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF.

ROLL CALL
City Council Members Present: Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zuckerman
City Council Member Absent:  Zerunyan

City Staff Present:  City Manager Doug Prichard
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  Community Services Director Andy Clark
  Planning Director David Wahba
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis
  Senior Planner Jeannie Naughton

Others Present:  Ritu Portugal, Park and Activities Commission

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

Players from the PVP Girls Softball League led the audience in the Pledge of Allegiance.

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

  NONE

5.  ROUTINE MATTERS

A.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF APRIL 11, 2017

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE THE CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF APRIL 11, 2017 AS
  PRESENTED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF SO ORDERED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS - APRIL

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE WARRANTS 58288 THROUGH 58325 FOR A GRAND
  TOTAL AMOUNT OF $333,025.20 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
APRIL 25, 2017
 6.  CONSENT CALENDAR: The following routine matters will be acted upon by one
  vote to approve with the majority consent of the City Council. There will be no
  separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior
  to the roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE ITEMS A-C.

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  Reading in full of all ordinances and resolutions presented for consideration to
  the City Council will be waived and all such ordinances and resolutions will be
  read by title only.

  APPROVED.

B.  MARCH 2017 SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

C.  MARCH MONTHLY REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF SO ORDERED.

7.  AUDIENCE ITEMS  NOT  ON  THE  AGENDA/WRITTEN  AND  ORAL
  COMMUNICATIONS

A.  LOS ANGELES COUNTY CLEAN ENERGY PRESENTATION

  Matt Skolnik, Los Angeles County, provided an extensive presentation of the
  Los Angeles Community Choice Energy Program which the Board of
  Supervisors has approved noting that cities are invited to participate.

  Following extensive discussion, City Manager Prichard noted that the Joint
  Powers Agreement will be presented to the COUNCIL at a future meeting.

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS/MEETINGS

  NONE

9.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF APRIL 17, 2017

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION
  MINUTES OF APRIL 17, 2017.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF SO ORDERED.

B.  ANNUAL AUDIT SERVICES AGREEMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the agreement and rates for
  the CPA firm of Macias Gini & O'Connell LLP to perform audit services for the
  Fiscal Year 2016-17, calculate and prepare the GASB #68 reports, prepare the
  State Controller's Cities Financial Transactions Report, prepare the Pepper Tree
  Foundation's tax returns, and review the GANN appropriation limitation.

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a staff report (as per
  agenda material).

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
APRIL 25, 2017
   COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE THE AGREEMENT AND RATES FOR THE CPA FIRM OF
  MACIAS GINI & O’CONNELL LLP TO PERFORM AUDIT SERVICES FOR
  THE FISCAL YEAR 2016-17, CALCULATE AND PREPARE THE GASB #68
  REPORTS, PREPARE THE STATE CONTROLLER’S CITIES FINANCIAL
  TRANSACTIONS REPORT, PREPARE THE PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION’S
  TAX RETURNS, AND REVIEW THE GANN APPROPRIATION LIMITATION.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

10.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  ORDINANCE NO. 717 - SECOND READING AND ADOPTION

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES ADDING CHAPTER 2.10 TO THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES
  MUNICIPAL CODE PERTAINING TO THE OFFICE OF THE CITY CLERK

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN

  TO ADOPT ORDINANCE NO. 717.

  City Manager Prichard read Ordinance No. 717 by title only.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

B.  ORDINANCE NO. 716 - REINTRODUCE FOR FIRST READING

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES PERTAINING TO SOCIAL HOST RESPONSIBILITY AND LIABILITY
  FOR HOSTING LOUD OR UNRULY GATHERINGS, INCLUDING THOSE WHERE
  UNDERAGE DRINKING OCCURS

  Recommendation: That the City Council receive any public testimony and
  introduce for first reading Ordinance No. 716.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material).

  City Attorney Davis noted a change under Section 9.10.030 regarding Civil
  Fines.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO REINTRODUCE ORDINANCE NO. 716 FOR FIRST READING AS
  AMENDED.

  City Manager Prichard read Ordinance No. 716 by title only.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF SO ORDERED.

C.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 18-16; NOTICE INVITING SEALED BIDS FOR
  STORM DRAIN IMPROVEMENTS ON JUNE’S TRAIL AT PALOS VERDES DRIVE
  EAST

  Recommendation: That the City Council authorize staff to solicit a notice
  inviting sealed bids for "Storm Drain Improvements on June's Trail," a public
  works project, under contract with Transtech Engineering.

  Planning Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
APRIL 25, 2017
   In response to COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ, David Ragland, Project Engineer,
  Transtech Engineers, noted that the grates will be eliminated and the catch
  basin will be located at the intersection and the east catch basin will be made
  larger to funnel the water.

  In response to COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN, Mr. Ragland noted that the pipe
  sizes are not the issue since the flooding is caused by a low capacity catch
  basin not being able to force the water through the pipes.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN inquired about the effect of this project on the
  City’s National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) obligations.
  Assistant City Manager Grammer noted that any improvements the City makes
  are recognized. Mr. Ragland noted that there is a component in the NPDES for
  bio retention.

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL, Mr. Ragland noted that the
  engineer’s estimate is for the actual work, i.e. construction cost.

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL’S inquiry regarding the Special
  Chandler Equestrian Contribution, Planning Director Wahba noted that
  currently there is about $800,000 available for equestrian-related purposes
  which this project will address.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL inquired about a possible conflict between the
  private trails owned by the Homeowners’ Association and another document
  stating that they are dedicated public trails. City Attorney Davis noted that the
  trails are open to the public even though they are privately owned with the
  dedications on title so the work being proposed would not be considered a gift of
  public funds.

  In response to COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN, City Manager Prichard noted that
  there will be a staff recommendation to award the job at a future meeting.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN

  TO AUTHORIZE STAFF TO SOLICIT A NOTICE INVITING SEALED BIDS
  FOR STORM DRAIN IMPROVEMENTS ON JUNE’S TRAIL, A PUBLIC
  WORKS  PROJECT,  UNDER  CONTRACT  WITH  TRANSTECH
  ENGINEERING.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

11.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

A.  City Attorney Davis noted that at the May 9 COUNCIL meeting, he will provide a
  Brown Act refresher course.

12.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS: This item provides the
  opportunity for Members of the City Council to provide information and reports to
  other Members of the City Council and/or the public on any issues or activities of
  currently active Council Committees, ad hoc committees, regional or state-wide
  governmental associations, special districts and/or joint powers authorities and
  their various committees on which Members of the City Council might serve or
  have an interest, which are not otherwise agendized.

A.  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL announced that the SCAG General Assembly will
  take place on May 4-5 for elected officials and city managers.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL noted that the Air Quality Management Plan was
  approved by the Air Resources Board.

B.  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL reported that she attended a meeting with the
  Palos Verdes Chamber of Commerce regarding economic development, and they
  are planning on offering a Fall Festival Wine Walk in October.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
APRIL 25, 2017
 13.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS: This item provides the opportunity for Members
  of the City Council to request information on currently pending projects and/or
  issues of public concern, direct that an item be agendized for future consideration
  and/or make announcements of interest to the public.

A.  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF announced that the Mayor’s Breakfast Ride is
  scheduled for Saturday, May 6 beginning at Chandler Park and ending at the
  Scout Pancake Breakfast at Howlett Park. She announced that breakfast tickets
  are available in advance for $3.00 at City Hall or $5.00 the day of the event at the
  park.

14.  CLOSED SESSION

  NONE

15.  ADJOURNMENT

  At 8:10 p.m. MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF formally adjourned the City Council
  meeting to May 1, 2017 at 5:00 p.m. for the purpose of a joint Adjourned City
  Council/Special Planning Commission meeting to discuss the General Plan
  Update.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Hope J. Nolan  Douglas R. Prichard
Deputy City Clerk  City Clerk

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
APRIL 25, 2017
